body:
I only just noticed that there was a PR addressing this issue already (#121748). 

However, there are two key differences:

PR #84199 appears to set `still_time = 0` in the `wake()` function. While this is reasonable, and may be the intended behaviour, it will add a performance hit for any case that wakes, because once a body wakes, it will stay awake for `SPACE_PARAM_BODY_TIME_TO_SLEEP`.

This PR (#121748) doesn't change the wake() function, but rather fixes a bug where waking would go back to sleep before ever testing for motion potential. So this PR:
* Will wake for one frame only when a constraint is added or removed, if there is no motion, it will sleep again
* Will not change the way wake() works currently

Since this issue has been long idle, it is worth adding some clarification:

It is my firm opinion that #64890 is a bug
* Sleeping is an optimisation, not a feature. Any change in simulation behaviour due to sleeping is unintended behaviour.
* This fix should have minimal impact on performance, while fixing a bug of omission and a timing bug.

I don't believe that there is any reasonable work around for this bug (except in limited circumstances).

On principle this approach looks pretty good.

I think on RC I mentioned that using a `bool` or tick counter might be slightly more bullet proof / easier to read than fudging a timer (in fact sleeping seems like something that might be better managed in ticks rather than seconds? I can't think of an obvious reason for using seconds but maybe I'm missing something).

Some other considerations:
* this fixes `GodotPhysics` but we might not be able to get the same behaviour in other backends, especially if this kind of thing is stored in thirdparty code, which we don't want to modify significantly
* performance - @jrouwe mentioned that performance when streaming in and out subparts of levels is something that we should consider. We may end up not wanting to wake up bodies during a `loading`, `unloading` phase (perhaps governed by an `alive` flag or similar).

Some similar discussion in #124422 which is proposing a manual API call for similar class of problems, that should work in all backends.

Ultimately though it would imo be a nice objective to have as much wakeup behaviour handled automatically as possible (providing it doesn't impact performance, particularly in streaming situations).
